key_insight: A physics-informed Fourier neural operator reconstructs unsteady 3D floating-turbine wakes from two observation planes and transfers learned wake dynamics from a 5 MW to a 22 MW turbine.
engineering_relevance: Sparse-measurement wake reconstruction could support downstream-inflow assessment in floating wind farms.
method: Generate fixed and coupled surge–pitch wakes using large-eddy simulation with an actuator line model.
Combine 4D spectral convolutions with continuity and rotor-forced momentum-residual regularization.
Train on 5 MW cases and fine-tune for cross-scale transfer to a 22 MW turbine.
evidence_signal: In simulation-based evaluation, 10% planar sampling nearly matched dense-input accuracy (relative L2 error 0.0689 versus 0.0684), while transfer learning reduced 22 MW streamwise-velocity error by 36% versus zero-shot inference at St = 0.6.
watch_item: Fine-scale vortex breakdown remains damped, and the abstract reports simulation-based rather than field validation.
paper_title: Three-Dimensional Wake Reconstruction and Cross-Scale Transfer for Floating Offshore Wind Turbines via Physics-Informed Fourier Neural Operators
